correctness.rationale: The boundary compression of (E−J_0)^−1 as E decreases to 2 is [[1,1],[1,2]], e.g. by the reflected free resolvent. Its positive-perturbation Birman–Schwinger compression has strictly decreasing eigenvalues above 2 (strict Loewner decrease on the two-dimensional supported subspace). Both limiting eigenvalues exceed 1 iff a>2 and b(a−2)>a−1. Equality creates no counted eigenvalue at the band edge: free oscillatory or affine tails at/in the band are not square summable except the zero tail, and a zero tail propagates back. Positivity excludes eigenvalues below −2, and Weyl's theorem gives the essential band. With u_j proportional to z^(j−1) on j≥1, the two boundary equations give 1−(a+b)z+abz²−bz³. The two simple interior zeros r<s are the eigenvalue parameters and F(1)>0 with negative leading coefficient forces the third zero t>1. Vieta gives the inverse quadratic and both parameter formulas; the existence of one admissible root, positive sum/product, and Q(1)≥(rs)²>0 force the second root above 1 as well, including multiplicity. Conversely reconstruction makes the cubic with roots r,s,t, hence exactly the stated spectrum. The separation formulas follow from the root difference and product. In local coordinates (p,t) with p=rs and t the simple exterior Jost root, the bound-energy coordinates are smoothly equivalent to (p,r+s), with r+s=1/t+pt/(1−p). The t derivative vanishes at the double inverse root with second derivative 2/t³>0; thus this is an actual nondegenerate fold. There p=1/(1+t²), a=t+2/t>2, b=t+1/t. Substitution gives the stated strictly monotone cubic threshold. The example follows from r=1/10, s=2/5; a fresh independent 100-site Sturm count checked both examples and sampled both sides of the fold threshold.
residual_risks: Finite sections corroborate the sample spectra only. The operator and inverse statements follow from the infinite-tail argument, not finite spectra.
